statement_record.book: The diagonal (constant-diagram) functor Δ : C ⟶ C^J has the colimit functor as a left adjoint and the limit functor as a right adjoint, Colim ⊣ Δ ⊣ Lim, whenever the J-indexed (co)limits exist; this is the adjoint characterization of (co)limits.
statement_record.intree: General Δ = Diagonal J : C ⟶ [J,C] (Functor/Diagonal.v:33); the binary special case Diagonal_Product C ⊣ ×(C) (Adjunction/Diagonal/Product.v:36); and Kan_Limit exhibiting Lim ≅ Ran(Erase J) F via ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran (Structure/Limit/Kan/Extension.v).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the general J-indexed adjunction Colim ⊣ Δ ⊣ Lim is not an in-tree theorem. Only the binary (co)product special case (J discrete of size 2) is a genuine adjunction. Limits/colimits are existence classes (Structure/Limit.v's Limit), not functors [J,C] ⟶ C adjoint to Δ. The Kan route yields Lim ≅ Ran(Erase J) F pointwise via ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran, but that is stated as precomposition ⊣ Ran under a standing RightKan hypothesis, not literally as Δ ⊣ Lim, and gives no Colim ⊣ Δ statement.

gap: The general adjoint characterization Colim ⊣ Δ ⊣ Lim for an arbitrary diagram shape J is not established as a theorem. There is no in-tree Lim/Colim functor [J,C] ⟶ C carrying an adjunction to the diagonal Δ : C ⟶ [J,C]; limits/colimits exist only as the per-diagram existence class Limit F. The general fact appears only in prose (Functor/Diagonal.v:30, Instance/Fun.v:70, Structure/Limit.v:80-82). Present concretely: the binary product adjunction Δ ⊣ × (and the Kan-extension form Induced ⊣ Ran giving Lim pointwise).

statement_record.intree: rapl_is_alimit (right adjoints preserve limits); AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows (universal arrows at every object ⟹ a left adjoint); Comma_Complete (comma category is complete under C complete + U preserves image-limits); GAFT (Adjunction/GAFT.v:241): Complete C + PreservesImageLimit U + a SolutionSet at each d ⟹ { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the forward conjunct (i) is exactly RAPL (rapl_is_alimit) and is fully proven. The reverse direction is available only through the universal-arrow engine (AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows), whose in-tree source of universal arrows is GAFT — the size-repaired Freyd theorem requiring the STRONGER hypotheses 'C complete + a solution set at each object' and Freyd's product-then-equalizer construction, not Theorem 2's hypothesis (ii) 'the comma projection has a limit'. Theorem 2's distinctive construction Fx = Lim(Q : (x↓G) ⟶ A) and its underlying Lemma-1 lifting (a limit of the comma projection is an initial object of the comma) are absent, and the biconditional is not stated as a formal criterion.
